what.text: This page follows refugees from the Central African Republic living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 201324 there, 29.9% of all Central African refugees.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of the Central African Republic in several periods since 2001.
From 2009 to 2014 the groups fighting the government include the CPJP, Seleka and anti-Balaka; from 2017 to 2025 they include anti-Balaka, the UPC and the CPC.

when.text: UNHCR's figure rose from 26549 in 2001 to a peak of 212630 in 2021.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2015 and 2017 to 2025, after big changes between 2011 and 2013.
Returns from the Democratic Republic of the Congo were highest in 2017 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees in the Democratic Republic of the Congo only, and UNHCR adds notes to some of them.
People displaced inside the Central African Republic are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
